claims.claim_text: Bell military aircraft and support programs revenue rose 28% to $2.618B in 2025, primarily on higher volume on the MV-75 program (the Army's V-280-based Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft).
claims.subject: Bell segment / MV-75 program
claims.predicate: drove 2025 military revenue growth and is the primary forward growth driver
claims.object_value: MV-75 (FLRAA / V-280) — $2.618B Bell military revenue in 2025, +$570M YoY
claims.source_quote: Bell's military aircraft and support programs revenues increased $570 million, 28%, in 2025, compared with 2024, primarily due to higher volume on the MV-75 program and military sustainment programs.

claims.claim_text: Textron expects to be awarded the long-lead Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phase of the MV-75/FLRAA contract in late 2026 or early 2027, with a $1.3 billion prototype testing & evaluation award already in backlog.
claims.subject: MV-75 program pipeline
claims.predicate: expects LRIP award in late 2026 / early 2027
claims.object_value: LRIP award timing; $1.3B prototype T&E new order; +$326M Bell backlog YoY
claims.source_quote: As the MV-75 program continues to accelerate, we expect that we will be awarded the long-lead Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phase of the contract in late 2026 or early 2027... New orders included a $1.3 billion award for the prototype testing and evaluation phase of the MV-75 program.

claims.claim_text: The Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft (FARA) program — for which Bell had been a competitor — wound down, materially lowering 2024 Bell R&D and producing a $56M Bell R&D increase year-over-year in 2025.
claims.subject: FARA program (Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft)
claims.predicate: program wound down; affected Bell R&D trajectory
claims.object_value: FARA wind-down; Bell R&D +$56M (58%) in 2025 vs 2024
claims.source_quote: Bell's research and development costs increased $56 million, 58%, in 2025, compared with 2024, largely reflecting lower costs in 2024 due to the wind down of the Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft program.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems' Shadow UAS program was cancelled and certain U.S. Government development programs were terminated, lowering Systems volume and mix in 2025.
claims.subject: RQ-7 Shadow UAS / Textron Systems development programs
claims.object_value: Shadow cancellation; certain DoD development programs terminated; offset by Ship-to-Shore Connector volume
claims.source_quote: The decrease in volume and mix largely reflects the impact of the cancellation of the Shadow program and termination of certain U.S. Government development programs, partially offset by higher volume on the Ship-to-Shore Connector program.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems' backlog grew 27% to $3.304B, including $480M for additional units on the Ship-to-Shore Connector (SSC) program and $475M for a five-year ATAC U.S. Navy Fighter Jet Services contract.
claims.subject: Ship-to-Shore Connector + ATAC Navy Fighter Jet Services
claims.object_value: Textron Systems backlog +$710M YoY to $3.304B; SSC $480M new orders; ATAC $475M 5-year contract
claims.source_quote: Textron Systems backlog increased $710 million, 27%, in 2025, compared with 2024, reflecting orders in excess of revenues recognized and deliveries. New orders included $480 million for additional units on the Ship-to-Shore Connector program and $475 million for a five-year contract for ATAC's U.S. Navy Fighter Jet Services.

claims.claim_text: Approximately 27% of Textron's 2025 revenues (~$4.0B) were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government, including foreign military sales — making U.S. Government defense spending a load-bearing driver of consolidated results.
claims.subject: DoD / U.S. Government customer concentration
claims.object_value: 27% of 2025 revenue (~$3.996B of $14.799B) from U.S. Government / FMS contracts
claims.source_quote: Approximately 27% of our 2025 revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government, including those under the U.S. Government-sponsored foreign military sales program.

claims.claim_text: On the upcoming MV-75 LRIP award, Textron expects an unfavorable cumulative catch-up program adjustment of $60-$110M reflecting higher-than-anticipated costs vs. original bid, though the overall MV-75 program will continue to generate positive margin.
claims.subject: MV-75 LRIP cost overrun risk
claims.predicate: expects unfavorable cum-catch-up adjustment of $60-$110M on LRIP award
claims.object_value: $60M-$110M unfavorable cum-catch-up upon LRIP award (fixed-price LRIP)
claims.source_quote: Upon award of the LRIP option, which is largely fixed price, we expect to record an unfavorable cumulative catch-up program adjustment, reflecting higher costs than originally anticipated from when the program was bid, in the range of $60 million to $110 million.

claims.claim_text: Textron Aviation (commercial) delivered 171 Citation jets and 146 commercial turboprops in 2025, generating $5.955B of revenue (+13%) — a non-J-Book commercial cohort that should remain stable regardless of DoD program funding.
claims.subject: Textron Aviation commercial (Cessna Citation)
claims.predicate: commercial backlog and deliveries drove segment growth
claims.object_value: 171 Citation jets + 146 turboprops in 2025; segment revenue $5.955B; backlog $7.724B
claims.source_quote: We delivered 171 Citation jets and 146 commercial turboprops in 2025, compared with 151 Citation jets and 127 commercial turboprops in 2024.

claims.claim_text: Textron operates 57 U.S. plants and 45 plants outside the U.S. (102 total) with approximately 23.8 million square feet of manufacturing space, of which 59 are owned.
claims.subject: Textron manufacturing footprint
claims.object_value: 57 U.S. + 45 ex-U.S. plants = 102; ~23.8M sq ft; 59 owned
claims.source_quote: On January 3, 2026, we operated a total of 57 plants located throughout the U.S. and 45 plants outside the U.S. We own 59 plants and lease the remainder for a total manufacturing space of approximately 23.8 million square feet.

claims.claim_text: Textron Specialized Vehicles divested its Powersports business in April 2025, reducing Industrial revenue by $195M and contributing to a $302M (9%) Industrial segment revenue decline.
claims.subject: Powersports divestiture
claims.object_value: -$195M FY25 revenue impact at Specialized Vehicles from Powersports disposition
claims.source_quote: Textron Specialized Vehicles' revenues decreased $294 million, 18%, largely reflecting a $195 million impact from the disposition of the Powersports business in April 2025... and lower volume and mix, primarily in golf products.
